enonce_markdown:
A solid block of aluminium has a mass of $540\ \mathrm{g}$ and a volume of $200\ \mathrm{cm^3}$.

What is the density of aluminium, in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Density is mass per unit volume: $\rho = \dfrac{m}{V}$. Remember the conversion $1\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}} = 1000\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$.

### Solution

$\rho = \dfrac{m}{V} = \dfrac{540\ \mathrm{g}}{200\ \mathrm{cm^3}} = 2.7\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$.

Conversion: $2.7\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}} = 2.7 \times 1000\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}} = 2700\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$.

(Check in SI units: $m = 0.540\ \mathrm{kg}$ and $V = 200\times10^{-6}\ \mathrm{m^3} = 2.0\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m^3}$, so $\rho = \dfrac{0.540}{2.0\times10^{-4}} = 2700\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$.)

Wrong options: $370$ is $V/m$ (inverted formula); $27\,000$ and $2.7\times10^{6}$ use wrong conversion factors.

**Answer: 2700 kg m$^{-3}$.**

enonce_markdown: A solid has a density of $1.2\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$. The solid is placed in each of the following liquids in turn. In which liquid does it float?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

A solid floats in a liquid if its density is smaller than the density of the liquid. It sinks if its density is greater than that of the liquid.

### Solution

The solid has density $1.2\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$.

- Kerosene ($0.80$): $1.2 > 0.80$, the solid sinks.
- Palm oil ($0.91$): $1.2 > 0.91$, the solid sinks.
- Water ($1.00$): $1.2 > 1.00$, the solid sinks.
- Mercury ($13.6$): $1.2 < 13.6$, the solid floats.

**Answer: mercury.**

enonce_markdown:
A student finds the density of an irregular stone. The stone has a mass of $156\ \mathrm{g}$. She pours water into a measuring cylinder and reads $50\ \mathrm{cm^3}$. She then lowers the stone gently into the water so that it is completely covered, and the reading becomes $110\ \mathrm{cm^3}$.

What is the density of the stone, in $\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The volume of an irregular solid is found by displacement: it equals the rise in the water level, $V = V_{\text{final}} - V_{\text{initial}}$. The density is then $\rho = \dfrac{m}{V}$.

### Solution

Volume of the stone: $V = 110 - 50 = 60\ \mathrm{cm^3}$.

Density: $\rho = \dfrac{m}{V} = \dfrac{156\ \mathrm{g}}{60\ \mathrm{cm^3}} = 2.6\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$ (that is, $2600\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$).

Wrong options: $1.4$ divides by the final reading ($156/110$); $3.1$ divides by the initial reading ($156/50$); $0.38$ inverts the formula.

**Answer: 2.6 g cm$^{-3}$.**

enonce_markdown:
A student measures the density of palm oil. An empty beaker has a mass of $150\ \mathrm{g}$. She pours $200\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of palm oil into the beaker, and the beaker and oil together have a mass of $332\ \mathrm{g}$.

(a) Calculate the mass of the palm oil. *[1 mark]*

(b) Calculate the density of palm oil in $\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$ and in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$. *[3 marks]*

(c) Calculate the mass, in kg, of $5.0$ litres of palm oil. ($1\ \text{litre} = 1000\ \mathrm{cm^3}$) *[2 marks]*

(d) Will palm oil float on water (density $1000\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$)? Give a reason. *[1 mark]*
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The mass of a liquid is found by subtracting the mass of the empty container. Then $\rho = \dfrac{m}{V}$ and $m = \rho V$. A less dense liquid floats on a denser one.

### Solution

**(a)** $m = 332 - 150 = 182\ \mathrm{g}$.

**(b)** $\rho = \dfrac{m}{V} = \dfrac{182\ \mathrm{g}}{200\ \mathrm{cm^3}} = 0.91\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$.

$0.91\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}} = 0.91 \times 1000 = 910\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$.

**(c)** $5.0$ litres $= 5000\ \mathrm{cm^3}$.

$m = \rho V = 0.91\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}} \times 5000\ \mathrm{cm^3} = 4550\ \mathrm{g} = 4.55\ \mathrm{kg}$.

**(d)** Yes, palm oil floats on water, because its density ($910\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$) is less than the density of water ($1000\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$).

enonce_markdown:
A concrete slab is $4.0\ \mathrm{m}$ long, $0.50\ \mathrm{m}$ wide and $0.20\ \mathrm{m}$ thick. The density of the concrete is $2400\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$.

What is the mass of the slab?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

For a block, volume $V = \text{length} \times \text{width} \times \text{thickness}$ (in metres). The mass follows from the density: $m = \rho V$.

### Solution

Volume: $V = 4.0 \times 0.50 \times 0.20 = 0.40\ \mathrm{m^3}$.

Mass: $m = \rho V = 2400\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}} \times 0.40\ \mathrm{m^3} = 960\ \mathrm{kg}$.

Wrong options: $96$ uses $0.020\ \mathrm{m}$ for the thickness; $4800$ forgets the thickness (it uses only length $\times$ width); $6000$ divides the density by the volume.

**Answer: 960 kg.**

enonce_markdown:
A technician mixes $300\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of water (density $1.00\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$) with $200\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of ethanol (density $0.80\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$). Assume that the volume of the mixture is exactly the sum of the two volumes.

(a) Calculate the mass of the water and the mass of the ethanol. *[2 marks]*

(b) Calculate the density of the mixture in $\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$ and in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$. *[3 marks]*

(c) A wooden cube has a density of $950\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$. Will it float or sink in the mixture? Will it float or sink in pure water? Explain each answer. *[3 marks]*
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The density of a mixture is the total mass divided by the total volume, $\rho = \dfrac{m_1 + m_2}{V_1 + V_2}$. It is not the average of the two densities unless the volumes are equal. A solid floats in a liquid when its density is smaller than that of the liquid.

### Solution

**(a)** Water: $m = \rho V = 1.00 \times 300 = 300\ \mathrm{g}$.

Ethanol: $m = \rho V = 0.80 \times 200 = 160\ \mathrm{g}$.

**(b)** Total mass: $300 + 160 = 460\ \mathrm{g}$. Total volume: $300 + 200 = 500\ \mathrm{cm^3}$.

$\rho = \dfrac{460\ \mathrm{g}}{500\ \mathrm{cm^3}} = 0.92\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}} = 920\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$.

**(c)** In the mixture: the cube's density ($950\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$) is greater than the density of the mixture ($920\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$), so the cube **sinks**.

In pure water: $950 < 1000\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, so the cube **floats**.
